question: Frontex is working with the Warsaw School of Sport to establish a new training centre for members of the Standing Corps. Initially, 200 Category 1 officials will be trained there as part of what is referred to as the basic training programme. In future, additional courses will also be offered there.

According to the Commission, the Frontex Standing Corps had 6 757 members at the end of March 2025, with the former Category 4 (reserve for immediate deployment) having been abolished. By 2027, the total number is expected to mushroom to 10 000 members.

At the same time, the Commission is preparing a possible amendment to the European Border and Coast Guard Regulation in order to implement the Commission President’s political objective of increasing the size of the force to make it 30 000 strong. 1.
How many members of the four categories of the Standing Corps are currently undergoing recruitment or have been deployed, and how many of them are permanently employed by Frontex?
How far has the Commission progressed with the preparation of a legislative proposal to increase the Standing Corps’ staff to 30 000, and what is the current proportion allocated to each category?
What does the basic training programme at the new training centre in Warsaw entail, where exactly is it located, and what other courses are to be offered?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (5.1.2026) At the end of September 2025, the European Border and Coast Guard Agency (Frontex) reported 1 239 deployable category 1 (statutory staff employed by Frontex), 880 selected category 2 (staff seconded from Member States for a long term) and 4 946 nominated category 3 (staff from Member States provided to Frontex for short-term deployment).

The Commission plans to adopt a proposal amending the European Border and Coast Guard Regulation (EBCG Regulation)1 in 2026. It will be accompanied by an impact assessment. A call for evidence and a public consultation were carried out, with the public consultation being concluded on 27 November 2025.

The allocation between different categories of the standing corps for the year 2025, as established in Annex I of the EBCG Regulation, consists of 2 000 category 1, 1 000 category 2 and 5 000 category 3. As sub-question three falls under the responsibility of Frontex, the Commission has asked the Agency to provide an answer to the question raised by the Honourable Member.
The Commission will send the Agency’s reply to the Honourable Member as soon as possible.
1 Regulation (EU) 2019/1896 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 13 November 2019 on the
European Border and Coast Guard and repealing Regulations (EU) No 1052/2013 and (EU) 2016/1624, OJ L 295, 14.11.2019, p. 1–131.
